Project Results and Discussion: Milestone 1.1.1: Develop multi-phase model of the reactor that predicts boule surface temperature as a function of boule properties The growth rate of the Si vapor deposition reaction is primarily controlled by the temperature at the growth surface. To accurately predict the growth rate of the deposition reaction, we needed an accurate thermal model of the boule/reactor system. Radiation from the hot boule surface to the reactor walls is a key parameter that controls the temperature of the growth surface, and so a primary activity in the first two quarters was the development of a radiation model for implementation into the full solver model. A surface-to-surface radiation model has been set up and coupled with heat convection and conduction to capture the temperature at the bottom surface of the boule accurately. As the temperature varies across the surfaces of boule and reactor, each surface of the geometry is discretized into many small pieces, which is the surface element facet of the mesh, and the temperature on each of these small facets is assumed to be constant, therefore the calculated surface radiational flux on each of these small facets is constant. 1. Coupled Convection, Conduction, and Radiation simulation The radiation model was implemented model to be coupled with heat conduction and convection. In the model, we have boule domain, reactor domain, and fluid domain between the boule and reactor. The surface-to-surface radiation is happening between the outer boule surfaces and inner reactor surface while the gas filled between the boule and reactor is assumed to be transparent which means the radiational heat flux is not absorbed by the gas. The coupled simulation was conducted in FeniCSx [5].
